questions.question_text: Which word from the lesson best describes the shape of an orange?
options: Rectangular
Round
Triangular
Straight
questions.correct_answer: Round
questions.explanation: The lesson gives the example sentence 'An orange is round.' Round is one of the shape words taught, along with rectangular, curved, square, triangular and straight.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: A fish is covered with ______, and a sheep is covered with ______.
options: feathers / fur
scales / wool
hair / scales
wool / feathers
questions.correct_answer: scales / wool
questions.explanation: The lesson's animal coverings are: hair, feathers, skin, fur, scales and wool. A fish has scales and a sheep has wool.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: In 'Lost', what has happened to the passenger's luggage?
options: It was stolen at the airport
It has not arrived yet
It was sent to the wrong city
He left it on the plane from Paris
questions.correct_answer: It has not arrived yet
questions.explanation: The passenger says he has just got off the plane from Paris, but his luggage hasn't arrived yet. He has two suitcases to describe.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: How does June describe her lost twin sister Kate?
options: Taller than June, with short hair and a blue T-shirt
The same age as June, not as tall, a little bit fatter, with much longer hair
Older than June, with the same hair and a red dress
Shorter than June, with glasses and a green T-shirt
questions.correct_answer: The same age as June, not as tall, a little bit fatter, with much longer hair
questions.explanation: June says Kate is her twin sister, ten years old, the same age as her, not as tall as her, a little bit fatter, and her hair is much longer. Her T-shirt is red.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What is Rama?
options: A cross between a lion and a tiger
A cross between a male camel and a female llama
A cross between a wolf and a jackal
A cross between a horse and a donkey
questions.correct_answer: A cross between a male camel and a female llama
questions.explanation: The article says Rama the cama was born in Dubai in January 1998, a cross between a male camel and a female llama.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: According to the article, how is Rama different from a camel and from a llama?
options: She is bigger than a camel and smaller than a llama
She is bigger than a llama but not as big as a camel, and has the llama's valuable wool coat
She has no hump and lives in the mountains of South America
She is the same size as a camel and has the camel's hair coat
questions.correct_answer: She is bigger than a llama but not as big as a camel, and has the llama's valuable wool coat
questions.explanation: Rama has a hump on her back like her father, is bigger than a llama but not as big as a camel, and has the wool coat of the llama, which is very valuable, unlike the hair coat of the camel.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Choose the correct comparative sentence.
options: Hassan is older than me.
Hassan is more older than me.
Hassan is oldest than me.
Hassan is as older than me.
questions.correct_answer: Hassan is older than me.
questions.explanation: The lesson's example is 'Hassan is older than me.' The comparative form is 'older than', and the superlative is 'the oldest boy in the class'.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which sentence shows contrast in the way 'whereas' is used in the lesson?
options: Whereas Ahmed worked hard, his brother didn't.
Whereas Ahmed worked hard, and his brother worked hard too.
Ahmed worked hard whereas to pass his exam.
Whereas is used only at the end of a sentence.
questions.correct_answer: Whereas Ahmed worked hard, his brother didn't.
questions.explanation: The lesson says 'whereas' can be used to give the same meaning as 'but', only to describe opposites: 'Whereas Ahmed worked hard, his brother didn't.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which of these is a word for describing the weather in 'The countryside'?
options: A misty day
A rocky hill
A deep valley
A wide river
questions.correct_answer: A misty day
questions.explanation: The lesson teaches four weather phrases: rainy weather, a misty day, a sunny afternoon and a windy evening.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which pair correctly matches two countryside features from the lesson?
options: A stream is a mountain; a desert is a river
Farmland is land used for farming; a valley is low land between hills
A coastline is a hill; a desert is a stream
A river is a small stream; a hill is flat farmland
questions.correct_answer: Farmland is land used for farming; a valley is low land between hills
questions.explanation: The lesson's countryside words are: a stream, a mountain, farmland, a river, a coastline, a valley, a desert and a hill. Farmland is farming land and a valley is the low land between hills.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: In 'A drive in the countryside', where did the writer spend his holiday?
options: In Scotland
In Wales
In Yemen
In Ireland
questions.correct_answer: In Wales
questions.explanation: The text begins: 'Last year, I spent my holiday in Wales, where the scenery is wonderful.' He drives along the coast road.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027
questions.source_detail: Lesson: A drive in the countryside

questions.question_text: What happens to the river as the writer drives higher?
options: It gets wider and wider until it reaches the sea
It gets narrower and narrower until it is just a stream
It disappears underground
It joins the sea on the left
questions.correct_answer: It gets narrower and narrower until it is just a stream
questions.explanation: The writer says: 'I drove higher and higher and the river got narrower and narrower, until it was just a stream.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027
questions.source_detail: Lesson: A drive in the countryside

questions.question_text: According to Language review 2, what is the correct order of adjectives before a noun?
options: Colour, opinion, size, age, shape, nationality, material
Opinion, size/build, age, shape, colour, nationality, material
Material, nationality, colour, shape, age, size, opinion
Age, opinion, colour, size, shape, material, nationality
questions.correct_answer: Opinion, size/build, age, shape, colour, nationality, material
questions.explanation: The lesson lists the adjective order: 1 Opinion (good, bad, beautiful), 2 Size/build, 3 Age, 4 Shape, 5 Colour, 6 Nationality, 7 Material — e.g. 'a beautiful, old, Yemeni building'.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which sentence joins two actions correctly with the -ing form, as taught in the lesson?
options: The children ran out of school, laughing and shouting happily.
The children ran out of school, laugh and shout happily.
The children ran out of school, laughed and shouted happily.
The children ran out of school, to laugh and shouting happily.
questions.correct_answer: The children ran out of school, laughing and shouting happily.
questions.explanation: The lesson shows joining sentences with the -ing form: 'The children ran out of school. They were laughing and shouting happily.' becomes 'The children ran out of school, laughing and shouting happily.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: In 'A view from a window', what time does Jane open her bedroom curtains?
options: At five o'clock in the morning
At six o'clock in the morning
At seven o'clock in the morning
At eight o'clock in the morning
questions.correct_answer: At six o'clock in the morning
questions.explanation: The text says: 'It was six o'clock in the morning. Jane opened the curtains of her bedroom window and looked out.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027
questions.source_detail: Lesson: A view from a window

questions.question_text: How is Jane's description organised?
options: From near to far
From far to near
From left to right only
In no particular order
questions.correct_answer: From far to near
questions.explanation: Jane first describes the far-away horizon (a wall of white mist), then the wood a little bit nearer, then the field with cows, and finally the chickens just below her window — the description moves from far to near.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027
questions.source_detail: Lesson: A view from a window

questions.question_text: According to the lesson, what is usually left out of English-language newspaper headlines?
options: The verb 'to be', the articles a, an and the
All nouns and verbs
Numbers and dates
The names of people and places
questions.correct_answer: The verb 'to be', the articles a, an and the
questions.explanation: The lesson says headlines generally use shortened, simplified sentences: in English-language headlines, the verb 'to be', the articles a, an and the are often left out, and the present tense is used even when talking about the past or the future.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which word-formation example from the lesson is correct?
options: pain + killer = painkiller; hope + less = hopeless
dark + ness = darken; un + well = well
pain + less = painless; hope + killer = hopeless
dark + en = darkness; un + well = unwell
questions.correct_answer: pain + killer = painkiller; hope + less = hopeless
questions.explanation: The lesson's word-formation clues give: two known words make a new word (pain + killer = painkiller), suffixes (hope + less = hopeless, dark + en = darken) and prefixes (un + well = unwell).
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: In 'Today's news', what did the wind turbines on White Hill start to do?
options: They stopped working after a storm
They came into operation, providing power for over 600 homes
They were demolished to build a castle
They were moved to the south of England
questions.correct_answer: They came into operation, providing power for over 600 homes
questions.explanation: The Daily Post summary says: 'Wind Turbines Start Operation — These wind turbines on White Hill came into operation yesterday, providing power for over 600 homes.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: According to the Daily Post summary, what is the 'Arctic ice scare'?
options: The Arctic ice layer is half as thick as it was ten years ago
A ship was trapped in Arctic ice for ten years
The North Pole has completely melted
Scientists found a Roman dam under the ice
questions.correct_answer: The Arctic ice layer is half as thick as it was ten years ago
questions.explanation: The summary says: 'Arctic ice scare — The arctic ice layer is half as thick as it was ten years ago, a scientist working at the North Pole said yesterday.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: In Don's dream, what frightens him?
options: A spaceship landing in the field
Two men with horrible faces, one holding a gun, and he cannot move
A bird talking to him in the balloon
Falling from a kilometre high
questions.correct_answer: Two men with horrible faces, one holding a gun, and he cannot move
questions.explanation: Don dreams he is working in the fields with his brother when two men run towards them; one is holding a gun, and he and his brother want to run but cannot move. He calls it a nightmare.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What happens at the end of Debbie's dream?
options: She wakes up after falling off the bird's back from a kilometre high
She lands the balloon safely on a mountain
The bird tells her to climb back into the balloon
She flies over the sea and never wakes up
questions.correct_answer: She wakes up after falling off the bird's back from a kilometre high
questions.explanation: Debbie dreams of flying in a balloon, then on a bird's back over mountains and sea. She loses her hold on the bird's feathers, falls from a kilometre high, and wakes up.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Choose the correct passive sentence, as taught in Language review 3.
options: The police arrested a man for dangerous driving.
A man was arrested for dangerous driving.
A man arrested for dangerous driving.
The police was arrested a man.
questions.correct_answer: A man was arrested for dangerous driving.
questions.explanation: The lesson explains the passive makes the thing done more important than the person who does it: 'The police arrested a man for dangerous driving' becomes 'A man was arrested for dangerous driving.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which sentence uses 'be + to + infinitive' to talk about a future plan, as in the lesson?
options: The President is to meet the ambassador tomorrow.
The President met the ambassador yesterday.
The President is meeting the ambassador now.
The President has met the ambassador before.
questions.correct_answer: The President is to meet the ambassador tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The lesson says 'be + to + infinitive' is used to talk about future plans or forecasts, often in newspapers: 'The President is to meet the ambassador tomorrow.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: According to the definitions in 'Natural disasters', what is a famine?
options: A shortage of food, during which people sometimes starve
A mountain with a hole in the top
A very large wood that catches fire
A powerful storm with strong winds
questions.correct_answer: A shortage of food, during which people sometimes starve
questions.explanation: The lesson defines a famine as a shortage of food: 'During a famine, people sometimes starve, they die of hunger.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What causes an earthquake, according to the lesson?
options: Two plates moving along a fault line
Smoke rising from a volcano
A long period without rain
Deep water over normally dry land
questions.correct_answer: Two plates moving along a fault line
questions.explanation: The lesson explains the earth's crust is divided into plates; where two plates meet is a fault line, and two plates moving along a fault line causes an earthquake, during which the ground moves and shakes.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: In the newspaper report, how strong were the hurricane winds?
options: Over 100 kph
Over 240 kph
Over 500 kph
Over 50 kph
questions.correct_answer: Over 240 kph
questions.explanation: The report says the storm hit late on Tuesday evening and 'Winds of over 240 kph demolished all the wooden houses and tore the roofs off others.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: According to the report, what happened in the large towns of Central America?
options: Nearly three-quarters of all buildings were destroyed
Only the hospitals were damaged
The towns were not affected at all
All the roads were rebuilt in one day
questions.correct_answer: Nearly three-quarters of all buildings were destroyed
questions.explanation: The report says: 'In the large towns, nearly three-quarters of all buildings have been destroyed. In the countryside, whole villages, in which hundreds of people lived, have disappeared.' About 10,000 are feared dead.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which sentence uses the present perfect tense to describe the present situation, as in Language review 4?
options: The storm hit the area late on Tuesday evening.
The worst hurricane in living memory has caused terrible damage.
People stood around silently.
The house I used to live in is very old.
questions.correct_answer: The worst hurricane in living memory has caused terrible damage.
questions.explanation: The lesson says to use the present perfect tense to describe the present situation: 'The worst hurricane in living memory has caused terrible damage.' The past simple is for something that happened at a known time.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: In 'Sana'a Secondary School, to which I went when I was younger, is one of the biggest schools in the country', where is the preposition?
options: At the end of the relative clause
At the beginning of the relative clause, between commas
There is no preposition in the sentence
After the verb 'is'
questions.correct_answer: At the beginning of the relative clause, between commas
questions.explanation: The lesson contrasts the two kinds of relative clause: in a necessary-information clause the preposition is at the end ('the house I used to live in'), but in an additional-information clause it is at the beginning ('to which I went when I was younger') and the clause is written between commas.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: According to the Richter scale table in 'Armenia – 7, December 1988', what effect does an earthquake of more than 8.0 have?
options: Slight damage to buildings
Considerable damage to buildings
Great damage
Almost total damage
questions.correct_answer: Almost total damage
questions.explanation: The table says: More than 8.0 — Almost total damage; More than 7.4 — Great damage; 7.0–7.3 — Serious damage, metal bridges bent; 6.2–6.9 — Considerable damage; 5.5–6.1 — Slight damage.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What did the newsflashes report about the town of Spitak?
options: It was completely flattened, with about 20,000 killed
It was not damaged at all
It was hit by a flood, not an earthquake
Its people were evacuated before the earthquake
questions.correct_answer: It was completely flattened, with about 20,000 killed
questions.explanation: A newsflash at 15.00 says: 'Spitak completely flattened. Most of population — 20,000 — killed. In Leninakan, Armenia's largest city, thousands of people are homeless. One in five buildings destroyed.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What is 'work experience', as explained in the lesson?
options: A full-time permanent job after school
The chance to find out about different jobs by working at weekends or in school holidays
A training course at university
An interview for a job
questions.correct_answer: The chance to find out about different jobs by working at weekends or in school holidays
questions.explanation: The lesson says organisations help young people by offering them 'work experience' — the chance to find out about different jobs by working at the weekends or in the school holidays.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which work experience notice asks for someone with a driving licence?
options: WEO 8, the Ministry of Health office job
WEO 7, helping the Society for the Handicapped organise trips
WEO 5, the City TV station job
WEO 2, the Central Hospital job
questions.correct_answer: WEO 7, helping the Society for the Handicapped organise trips
questions.explanation: Notice WEO 7 says: 'Would you like to help the Society for the Handicapped organise trips for its members? You will take the members on trips yourself, so a driving licence is required. No experience is necessary.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What is Patrick's ambition, and what is his best subject?
options: To become a doctor; Biology
To become a teacher; Mathematics
To work in business; Sport
To become a social worker; History
questions.correct_answer: To become a doctor; Biology
questions.explanation: Patrick's ambition after leaving school is to become a doctor. His best subject is Biology and his worst is Mathematics. He has been going to first-aid evening classes and enjoys underwater swimming.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which person would most suit work helping other people as a social worker?
options: Justin, who likes driving and cooking
Fareeda, who is very helpful, takes old people shopping and wants to help other people
Clara, who collects folk-music CDs
Andrew, who has a driving licence and likes nature
questions.correct_answer: Fareeda, who is very helpful, takes old people shopping and wants to help other people
questions.explanation: Fareeda is described as very helpful and popular; at weekends she takes old people shopping in her parents' car, and she wants to help other people in some way, perhaps as a social worker.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: In 'Getting careers advice', what is the school-leaver good at?
options: Mathematics and Chemistry
History and Geography
English and Sport
Physics and Biology
questions.correct_answer: History and Geography
questions.explanation: The school-leaver says he is not good at Maths — 'I'm hopeless at it' — and when asked what he is good at, he answers 'History... and Geography... and that's it.' He has recently been working in a hospital and enjoys it very much.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which phrase is used in the lesson for TURNING DOWN advice?
options: That's a good idea.
If I were you, I would...
That's not a very good idea.
Can you help me, please?
questions.correct_answer: That's not a very good idea.
questions.explanation: The lesson's boxes give: Asking for advice — 'Can you help me, please?'; Accepting advice — 'That's a good idea'; Giving advice — 'If I were you, I would...'; Turning down advice — 'That's not a very good idea', 'I don't like doing that', 'I'm not good/very bad at that.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which sentence is in the present perfect continuous, as taught in Language review 5?
options: I have done my homework.
He has been playing football.
I have lived here for six years.
It began to rain.
questions.correct_answer: He has been playing football.
questions.explanation: The lesson's examples of the present perfect continuous are: 'He has been playing football', 'It has been raining', 'Mona has been studying English for six years' and 'The weather has been getting warmer recently.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What is the difference between 'I've read that book' and 'I've been reading that book' in the lesson?
options: The simple tense emphasises completion of the action; the continuous tense emphasises how long the action has been going on
The simple tense is about the future; the continuous is about the past
There is no difference in meaning
The continuous tense is only used with the verb 'read'
questions.correct_answer: The simple tense emphasises completion of the action; the continuous tense emphasises how long the action has been going on
questions.explanation: The lesson says the simple tense emphasises the completion of the action and can refer to actions that happened a long time ago, while the continuous tense emphasises how long the action has been going on and usually refers to something that has been happening recently.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which of these job names is a compound noun, as taught in 'Jobs and qualities'?
options: Teacher
Taxi-driver
Doctor
Nurse
questions.correct_answer: Taxi-driver
questions.explanation: The lesson says some job names combine two nouns into one word and are called compounds, for example taxi-driver. Sometimes they are joined (shopkeeper), sometimes hyphenated (life-guard), sometimes two words (English teacher).
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: If you want to be a teacher you must be patient. What noun does the employer ask for?
options: Politeness
Patience
Confidence
Ability
questions.correct_answer: Patience
questions.explanation: The lesson says: 'If you want to be a teacher you must be patient. In an advertisement the employer will ask for someone who shows patience.' The adjective–noun pairs include polite/politeness, patient/patience, confident/confidence and able/ability.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What does the Adult Education Development Worker job involve?
options: Teaching adults with learning difficulties in their own homes
Selling ice-cream to hospitals and hotels
Organising trips for the handicapped
Working in a hospital as a nurse
questions.correct_answer: Teaching adults with learning difficulties in their own homes
questions.explanation: The advertisement says the Ministry of Education is looking for a confident and well-educated individual to work locally, teaching adults with learning difficulties in their own homes. A driving licence is desirable and the successful applicant will have good communication skills, experience of teaching and be computer literate.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which applicant better fits the job's requirements, and why?
options: Tim Brook, because he has worked in adult education for two years
Kate Ash, because she is a qualified teacher with adult-education training, experience with adults with learning difficulties, computer experience and a driving licence
Neither applicant has any relevant experience
Both applicants are equally qualified in every way
questions.correct_answer: Kate Ash, because she is a qualified teacher with adult-education training, experience with adults with learning difficulties, computer experience and a driving licence
questions.explanation: Kate Ash is 24, a qualified Primary School teacher since 21, has had training in adult education, spent months teaching evening classes for adults with learning difficulties, has been using computers, and has recently passed her driving test. Tim Brook has adult-education experience and a driving licence but no experience of working on computers.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which preposition correctly follows 'interested', as taught in Language review 6?
options: interested for
interested in
interested of
interested to
questions.correct_answer: interested in
questions.explanation: The lesson lists words commonly followed by prepositions: nouns — training in, experience of, chance of; adjectives — interested in, grateful for; verbs — look forward to, applying for. They are always followed by a noun or a gerund.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which connecting word shows CONSEQUENCE in the lesson?
options: Furthermore
As well as
Consequently
Also
questions.correct_answer: Consequently
questions.explanation: For addition the lesson gives as well as, together with, as well/also, furthermore and in addition. For consequence it gives because, so, therefore, thus (followed by -ing), consequently, as a consequence, as a result, accordingly and that is why.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: If you begin a business letter with 'Dear Sir', how must you close it?
options: Yours sincerely
Yours faithfully
Best wishes
Love
questions.correct_answer: Yours faithfully
questions.explanation: The lesson's note says: if you use the greeting 'Dear Sir' or 'Dear Madam', you must use 'Yours faithfully' to close; if you use 'Dear Mr/Mrs Jones', you must use 'Yours sincerely'.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: According to the 'Fantastic Job Opportunity' advertisement, who are the newspaper looking for?
options: Experienced teachers over 25
Young men and women to train as reporters and photographers for a magazine for people under 25
Doctors for a new hospital
Drivers with a full licence
questions.correct_answer: Young men and women to train as reporters and photographers for a magazine for people under 25
questions.explanation: The advertisement says: 'We are looking for young men and women to train as reporters and photographers for a new general interest magazine for people under 25. No experience is necessary but the successful applicants must be willing to work hard and already have a wide range of interests.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which of these foods is a grain crop, according to 'Food'?
options: Sorghum
Mango
Fig
Grape
questions.correct_answer: Sorghum
questions.explanation: The lesson lists things grown in Yemen — dates, figs, mangoes, papayas, sorghum, apricots, grapes, pears — and asks 'What is a grain crop?' Sorghum is the grain crop among them.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What do you get if you squeeze a lemon, and which verb means to cut something into small pieces?
options: Lemon juice / chop
Lemon peel / grate
Lemon oil / grind
Lemon pulp / boil
questions.correct_answer: Lemon juice / chop
questions.explanation: The lesson's cooking verbs are boil, squeeze, peel, crush, grate, chop, grill and grind, and it asks 'What do you get if you squeeze a lemon?' — lemon juice. 'Chop' means to cut into small pieces.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: In 'Learning to cook', what is a loomi?
options: A mixture of spices
A small, dried lime
A kind of fish
A cooking pot
questions.correct_answer: A small, dried lime
questions.explanation: James's mother explains: 'It's a loomi — a small, dried lime.' Baharat, by contrast, is a mixture of spices.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What is the correct order of the main steps in making the fish curry?
options: Fry the fish first, then fry the onions and spices, then add water
Fry the onions and garlic, add the spices, add tomatoes and loomi, cover with water and simmer; fry the fish separately and add it to the sauce
Boil the fish in water, then add the raw spices
Add the spices to the raw fish, then boil everything together for fifteen minutes
questions.correct_answer: Fry the onions and garlic, add the spices, add tomatoes and loomi, cover with water and simmer; fry the fish separately and add it to the sauce
questions.explanation: The mother explains: fry the onions and garlic, add the spices and fry for a further two minutes, add the tomatoes, loomi, lemon juice, salt and pepper, cover with water and simmer for fifteen minutes. While the mixture is boiling gently, fry the fish pieces until golden brown, then put the fish into the sauce and simmer for a further fifteen minutes.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: According to 'Agriculture in Yemen', what is Yemen's most famous crop?
options: Cotton
Coffee
Sorghum
Dates
questions.correct_answer: Coffee
questions.explanation: The text says that in the highest parts of the slopes, with a moderate climate and rather cold winter nights, 'it is here that Yemen's most famous crop, coffee, is grown.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What grows in the Tihamah, the hot coastal zone of Northern Yemen?
options: Apples, pears and grapes
Dates and cotton, as well as vegetables and grains
Only coffee
Mangoes, papayas and bananas
questions.correct_answer: Dates and cotton, as well as vegetables and grains
questions.explanation: The Tihamah (sea level to 300m) has a tropical climate, hot and humid in summer. 'Dates and cotton grow well here, as do vegetables and grains, which are both a winter and summer crop.' Mangoes, papayas and bananas grow in Zone 2 (300–2,200m).
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Choose the correct passive form of 'People grow coffee in Yemen.'
options: Coffee grows in Yemen by people.
Coffee is grown in Yemen.
Coffee was growing in Yemen.
People are grown coffee in Yemen.
questions.correct_answer: Coffee is grown in Yemen.
questions.explanation: Language review 7 shows: 'People grow coffee in Yemen' becomes 'Coffee is grown in Yemen.' The passive is used when you want to make the object more important than the subject, and the original subject is often omitted.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly uses 'while' + present continuous with present simple to show two actions happening at the same time?
options: While the mixture is boiling gently, you fry the pieces of fish.
While the mixture boiled gently, you fried the pieces of fish yesterday.
While the mixture is boiling gently, you fried the pieces of fish.
While the mixture boils gently, you will fry the pieces of fish tomorrow.
questions.correct_answer: While the mixture is boiling gently, you fry the pieces of fish.
questions.explanation: The lesson's example is: 'While the mixture is boiling gently, you fry the pieces of fish.' — while + present continuous with the present simple shows two actions happening at the same time.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: According to 'Words and more words', which English words came from Arabic?
options: Table and dinner
Algebra and zero
Kayak and igloo
Blueberry and farmhouse
questions.correct_answer: Algebra and zero
questions.explanation: The text says English borrowed words from many languages: from Latin, Greek and French (table, dinner, medicine); kayak and igloo from the Eskimo language; and 'the Arabic words algebra and zero' came into English through contact with Arab mathematicians. Sugar, cotton and coffee also came from the Arab world through trade.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which word is made by combining two different words, as taught in the lesson?
options: Unhappy (prefix un- + happy)
Careless (care + -less)
Blueberry (blue + berry)
Comfortable (comfort + -able)
questions.correct_answer: Blueberry (blue + berry)
questions.explanation: The lesson lists four ways of making new words: borrowing, adding a prefix or suffix (re- in remake, -less in careless, -able in comfortable), combining two words (blue + berry = blueberry, farmhouse, handbag, newspaper), and changing how a word is used (milk as noun and verb).
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What was Aisha Yousif's hypothesis in her water-pressure experiment?
options: The deeper the water, the greater the pressure.
The thicker the dam, the weaker the pressure.
Water pressure is the same at every depth.
The top jet of water is always the longest.
questions.correct_answer: The deeper the water, the greater the pressure.
questions.explanation: Aisha's hypothesis was: 'The deeper the water, the greater the pressure.' Her question was why a dam is thicker at the bottom than at the top.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027
questions.source_detail: Lesson: Investigating the world around us

questions.question_text: What did Aisha's data show, and what did she conclude?
options: All four jets were the same length; the hypothesis was wrong
The jet at the top was the longest; pressure is greatest at the top
The jet at the bottom was the longest and the jet at the top the shortest, so the data confirmed the hypothesis
No water came out of any hole, so the experiment failed
questions.correct_answer: The jet at the bottom was the longest and the jet at the top the shortest, so the data confirmed the hypothesis
questions.explanation: Her data: 'Four jets of water came out of the bottle. The jet at the top was the shortest and the jet at the bottom was the longest. The other two jets were in-between.' Her conclusion: the length of the jet is related to the pressure of the water — the greater the pressure, the longer the jet — so the data confirms the hypothesis.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027
questions.source_detail: Lesson: Investigating the world around us

questions.question_text: In Language review 8, which sentence correctly uses 'have' + infinitive to give an instruction?
options: Have the boy to put away his bag.
Have the boy put away his bag.
Have the boy putting away his bag.
Have the boy puts away his bag.
questions.correct_answer: Have the boy put away his bag.
questions.explanation: The lesson says have/get + infinitive replace instruction words such as ask, tell or order. With 'have', the infinitive is WITHOUT 'to': 'Have the boy put away his bag.' (With 'get' it is 'Get the boy to put away his bag.')
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which sentence uses two comparatives to show how one action causes the other, as in the lesson?
options: The water is deeper than the dam.
The deeper the water, the greater the pressure.
The pressure is greater at the bottom.
Water pressure increases with depth.
questions.correct_answer: The deeper the water, the greater the pressure.
questions.explanation: The lesson teaches two comparatives, one in each half of the sentence, to show how one action causes the other: 'The deeper the water, the greater the pressure' and 'The further you go down, the more your ears hurt.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Why are frozen peas fresher than the peas you buy in the market?
options: Because they are picked when they are hard
Because they are processed within two or three hours of being picked, while ordinary peas take many hours or even days to reach the shops
Because they are stored at -18°C for months
Because they are washed in salt water
questions.correct_answer: Because they are processed within two or three hours of being picked, while ordinary peas take many hours or even days to reach the shops
questions.explanation: The text says frozen peas are fresher because they are processed within two or three hours of being picked or harvested. Ordinary peas are first sent to the market and then on to shops, which can take many hours or even days, and all this time the peas are getting less and less fresh.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What is 'blanching' in the frozen-pea process?
options: Cooling the peas to less than 20°C
Packing the peas into big bags
Passing the peas through boiling water for one minute, or through steam for two or three minutes
Choosing the softer peas for freezing
questions.correct_answer: Passing the peas through boiling water for one minute, or through steam for two or three minutes
questions.explanation: The process: the softer peas are chosen for freezing and the harder ones kept for canning; the peas are cleaned by fans, washed, then 'passed through boiling water for one minute, or through steam for two or three minutes, a process known as blanching.' Then they are cooled to less than 20°C, passed through salt water or brine, washed again and quick-frozen.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: In 'Word sets', what do we call a group of connected words such as table, sofa, chair and armchair?
options: A word set
A sentence
A paragraph
A spelling list
questions.correct_answer: A word set
questions.explanation: The lesson says: 'A group of connected words is called a word set.' Table, sofa, chair and armchair are all pieces of furniture, so they belong to the same word set.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which of these words belongs to the harbour word set in the lesson?
options: Armchair
Telescope
Sofa
Table
questions.correct_answer: Telescope
questions.explanation: The harbour picture's word set includes mast, pulling up the sail, rowing, deck, cabin, horizon, climbing aboard, bow, oar, telescope, fishing boat, tanker, stern and net. Armchair, sofa and table belong to the furniture word set.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: The children find an object with a number on it. Which sentence shows they are now CERTAIN what it is?
options: It might be a coin.
It may be a piece of jewellery.
It must be a coin.
It could be an earring.
questions.correct_answer: It must be a coin.
questions.explanation: The lesson says may/might/could express possibilities, but 'must' expresses certainty. When the children see the number on the object, they say: 'No, look. There is a number here. It must be a coin.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What would happen if there was no more rain in Yemen, according to the lesson's example?
options: The whole country would turn to desert.
The rivers would become wider.
People would move to the coast.
The farmland would produce more food.
questions.correct_answer: The whole country would turn to desert.
questions.explanation: The lesson's example answer is: 'If there was no more rain in Yemen, the whole country would turn to desert.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Who says: 'Can anybody tell me the name of the highest mountain in Africa?'
options: A firefighter
A teacher
A farmer
A tour guide
questions.correct_answer: A teacher
questions.explanation: In the lesson's puzzle, only one answer is possible for each speaker. 'Can anybody tell me the name of the highest mountain in Africa?' is the question of a teacher asking a class.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What is the answer to this riddle: 'North, south, east or west — I'll show you where they are.'?
options: A calculator
A parachute
A compass
A football
questions.correct_answer: A compass
questions.explanation: The riddle object that shows north, south, east and west is a compass. The other riddles in the lesson are a football ('People kick me all the time...'), a calculator ('Without me you have to do your Mathematics homework in your head') and a parachute ('Hold me, jump off a mountain and fly like a bird').
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly uses 'must not' to forbid something, as taught in Language review 9?
options: You must not look at your books during an exam.
It must not be a toothbrush.
You must not be able to swim.
It must not rain tomorrow.
questions.correct_answer: You must not look at your books during an exam.
questions.explanation: The lesson says 'must not' is only used when you tell somebody they are not allowed to do something: 'You must not look at your books during an exam.' For negative certainty we use 'can't': 'It can't be a toothbrush.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What is the difference between 'I saw the goats coming down the street' and 'I saw the goats come down the street'?
options: The -ing form emphasises the action was continuous; the infinitive emphasises the action was completed
The -ing form is past tense; the infinitive is present tense
There is no difference in meaning
The -ing form is wrong after 'saw'
questions.correct_answer: The -ing form emphasises the action was continuous; the infinitive emphasises the action was completed
questions.explanation: The lesson says sense verbs (see, hear, feel) are followed by object + verb. The -ing form emphasises the action was continuous ('I saw the goats coming down the street'), while the infinitive emphasises the action was completed ('I saw the goats come down the street').
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: On what date did Captain Morehouse of the Dei Gratia sight the Mary Celeste?
options: 5th December 1872
5th December 1873
7th December 1888
5th November 1872
questions.correct_answer: 5th December 1872
questions.explanation: The text begins: 'On 5th December 1872, Captain Morehouse of the Dei Gratia was sailing from New York to Gibraltar... at about nine o'clock in the morning, they sighted another ship.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027
questions.source_detail: Lesson: The mystery of the Mary Celeste

questions.question_text: What did Captain Morehouse find when he boarded the Mary Celeste?
options: The ship was completely deserted, but everything was in place and nothing had been taken
The crew had been killed by pirates
The ship was sinking and the lifeboats were gone
The captain's cabin had been robbed of gold and jewellery
questions.correct_answer: The ship was completely deserted, but everything was in place and nothing had been taken
questions.explanation: The ship was deserted — nobody on deck, no one at the wheel — but in the cabins everything was in place, food was hanging over a dead fire and a half-eaten meal was on the table. Captain Morehouse found gold, jewellery and money on board: nothing had been taken and there was no sign of panic.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027
questions.source_detail: Lesson: The mystery of the Mary Celeste

questions.question_text: Which of these is one of the possible explanations given for the Mary Celeste mystery?
options: Pirates may have attacked the ship and sold the crew as slaves
The crew were rescued by a passing submarine
The ship was hit by a meteor
The crew flew away in a balloon
questions.correct_answer: Pirates may have attacked the ship and sold the crew as slaves
questions.explanation: The lesson lists five possible explanations: a huge monster dragged the people into the water; an island appeared and sank; a hurricane blew everybody off the ship; the people caught a terrible disease and drowned themselves; pirates attacked the ship, took the crew and passengers and sold them as slaves.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which modal verb does the lesson use to express a possibility about the past, as in 'A hurricane ___ have blown everybody off the ship'?
options: must
could
will
shall
questions.correct_answer: could
questions.explanation: The lesson's explanations use may/might/could + have + past participle for past possibilities: 'A huge monster may have come up out of the sea', 'An island might have appeared suddenly', 'A hurricane could have blown everybody off the ship.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: In reported speech, what does 'will' become?
options: Would
Could
Should
Might
questions.correct_answer: Would
questions.explanation: Language review 10 shows the changes in reported speech: 'will' becomes 'would' and 'can' becomes 'could'; the simple past and the past perfect both become the past perfect.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly reports a suggestion using 'suggest + -ing'?
options: I suggested to take a taxi.
I suggested taking a taxi.
I suggested that taking a taxi.
I suggested took a taxi.
questions.correct_answer: I suggested taking a taxi.
questions.explanation: The lesson says: 'The verb suggest can be followed by the -ing form of the verb: I suggested taking a taxi.' It can also be followed by 'that + subject + should + infinitive': 'The Captain suggested that the sailors should search the ship.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: In 'Tracks in the sand', what did the narrator see the man do on the train?
options: He took a gun out of his pocket, waved it, and jumped off the train as it was going round a bend
He bought a ticket and sat down quietly
He fell asleep in his seat
He spoke to the woman sitting next to him
questions.correct_answer: He took a gun out of his pocket, waved it, and jumped off the train as it was going round a bend
questions.explanation: The narrator says: 'I saw him take a gun out of his pocket. He waved it... and jumped off the train as it was going round a bend.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What did the tracks in the sand show the narrator?
options: The footprints of only one man, leading out of the village into the desert
The footprints of a large group of people going to the town
Tyre tracks of a car going to the railway station
No footprints at all, because the wind had covered them
questions.correct_answer: The footprints of only one man, leading out of the village into the desert
questions.explanation: The narrator followed the tracks: 'They led out of the village into the desert. The footprints were those of one man only.' A woman in the village also said she had seen someone going off in the direction of the tracks.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which headline matches the story of Mrs Khalifa Al-Tamari and her two children?
options: DRIVERS INJURED IN HIGHWAY CRASH AND FIRE
HIT-AND-RUN DRIVER INJURES STUDENT
FAMILY SAVED FROM BURNING HOME
CASTLE TO GO
questions.correct_answer: FAMILY SAVED FROM BURNING HOME
questions.explanation: Mrs Khalifa Al-Tamari, her son Amri (5) and daughter Shareefa (2) were rescued from a fire in their flat in Medina Road. Her husband Mustapha, helped by Fire Officer Nasser Badawi, carried his wife and children to safety.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What happened to Alia Nawaz, 18, in Harib Street?
options: She was rescued from a burning flat
She was badly injured when a blue Suzuki jeep hit her and drove straight on
She was saved by two fire engines
She was treated for burns on her arms
questions.correct_answer: She was badly injured when a blue Suzuki jeep hit her and drove straight on
questions.explanation: The article says: 'Alia Nawaz, 18, was badly injured yesterday in a horrific accident in Harib Street. Walking home from school at 1.30, she was hit by a blue Suzuki jeep which drove straight on.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: In 'A lucky escape', how should you start describing the picture?
options: With the things in the foreground
With the things furthest away
With the people on the right
With the nearest car
questions.correct_answer: With the things furthest away
questions.explanation: The lesson says: 'Look at the picture. Then describe it using words that you collected in your Workbook in the last lesson and the language below. Start with the things furthest away.' The language is: 'In the distance, you can see... Nearer us, there's... In the foreground, there are...'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which headline from page 41 fits the picture in 'A lucky escape'?
options: FAMILY SAVED FROM BURNING HOME
HIT-AND-RUN DRIVER INJURES STUDENT
DRIVERS INJURED IN HIGHWAY CRASH AND FIRE
WIND TURBINES START OPERATION
questions.correct_answer: DRIVERS INJURED IN HIGHWAY CRASH AND FIRE
questions.explanation: The lesson asks learners to 'choose and read out the correct headline from page 41'. The picture shows a highway crash scene on a mountain road with a lorry, a car, a police car and injured people, which fits 'DRIVERS INJURED IN HIGHWAY CRASH AND FIRE'.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What turned an ordinary job into a terrifying incident for Anwar at Jebel Kebir?
options: A large rock started to roll, and hundreds and thousands of bees rose from the hives
A fire broke out in the farmhouse
A flood washed away the road
A snake bit Anwar on the hand
questions.correct_answer: A large rock started to roll, and hundreds and thousands of bees rose from the hives
questions.explanation: Anwar and his father Kassim were nearly finished with the line of beehives when they heard a loud crash: a large rock was starting to roll, other rocks rolled and bounced down, and 'hundreds and thousands of bees rose from the hives.' Anwar tripped and fell, and his hat and face covering fell off.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Why did the incident become a major medical emergency, and where did Salwa decide to take Anwar?
options: Anwar broke his leg; to the clinic in the village
Anwar had been stung hundreds of times and was almost unconscious; to the hospital in Hajjah
Anwar had lost a lot of blood; to Tripoli Central Hospital
Anwar could not breathe; to the fire station
questions.correct_answer: Anwar had been stung hundreds of times and was almost unconscious; to the hospital in Hajjah
questions.explanation: Salwa Mafous, the District Nurse, said: 'He's been stung hundreds of times... I've never seen anything like it!' Then she held his wrist to check his pulse: 'Quick! We must get him to hospital in Hajjah.' She put Anwar on the back seat of her car and drove away at high speed.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What is the task in 'Saving Anwar'?
options: To read a text about Anwar and answer questions
To listen to a conversation and number the pictures in the order you hear them
To write a letter to the hospital
To act out the accident at Jebel Kebir
questions.correct_answer: To listen to a conversation and number the pictures in the order you hear them
questions.explanation: The lesson says: 'Listen to the conversation. In Workbook activity A, number the pictures in the order you hear them.' The pictures show stages of saving Anwar, such as the drive to hospital and treatment in the hospital.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: In 'How a hospital works', who are put on the 'fast track'?
options: People with less serious injuries, who wait longer
Patients who come by ambulance with a bad injury, such as from a bad car crash
Patients who only need an X-ray
Visitors who come with a patient
questions.correct_answer: Patients who come by ambulance with a bad injury, such as from a bad car crash
questions.explanation: The visitor explains: 'We have a two-track system. We put people with really bad injuries on the 'fast track'. They're patients who come in by ambulance from a bad car crash, for example, or people like Anwar. They're the highest priorities, of course, and they get immediate treatment.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What does the reception nurse do in the casualty process?
options: She registers the patient's personal details
She examines each patient and gives a priority — red for bad injuries and for young children and old people, blue for less serious injuries
She sends the patient for an X-ray
She drives the ambulance
questions.correct_answer: She examines each patient and gives a priority — red for bad injuries and for young children and old people, blue for less serious injuries
questions.explanation: After the receptionist registers personal details, 'the reception nurse... quickly examines each patient and gives each one a priority — red for bad injuries and also for young children and old people, and blue for people with less serious injuries.' She adds her notes to the registration form and sends it to the team of doctors.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Which job does the district nurse do, according to 'Working in public service'?
options: She works at the main entry port for Hajjis, helping people with cultural and social problems
She visits several villages each week, deals with major health problems, sends people to hospital in Hajjah and does health education
She plans the rebuilding of the city centre
She teaches English at a school
questions.correct_answer: She visits several villages each week, deals with major health problems, sends people to hospital in Hajjah and does health education
questions.explanation: The third speaker says: 'Before, there was no health care in the area. I've been working here for eight years now, and things have really improved. I visit several each week, and I deal with more major problems... I also do a lot of health education. I feel good that we've reduced death and disease so much.' This is the district nurse.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What do all three people in 'Working in public service' like about their work?
options: They all earn a very high salary
They all like helping to make life better for other people
They all work in the same hospital
They all travel to other countries
questions.correct_answer: They all like helping to make life better for other people
questions.explanation: The lesson ends with: 'Discuss what all these people like about their work.' Each speaker describes helping others: rebuilding the city to make life better for everyone, helping people with their problems, and improving health care and reducing death and disease.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Why did Dr Suleiman Badawi decide to become a doctor in 1960?
options: He wanted to earn a high salary in Tripoli
His friend Sadiq died of tuberculosis and his sister Fareeda was dying too, while the nearest doctor was 200 kilometres away
He was asked to run the Trachoma Centre in Benghazi
He wanted to study in Cairo
questions.correct_answer: His friend Sadiq died of tuberculosis and his sister Fareeda was dying too, while the nearest doctor was 200 kilometres away
questions.explanation: Dr Badawi says: 'I remember the day in 1960 when I decided to become a doctor. I was 16, and two months earlier a good friend of mine, Sadiq, had died of tuberculosis. Now it seemed my younger sister, Fareeda, was going to die too... the nearest doctor was 200 kilometres away.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027
questions.source_detail: Lesson: Huge changes in Libyan health care

questions.question_text: What happened in Dr Badawi's life in 1973, and what has Libya now stopped?
options: He became Senior Surgeon at Tripoli Central Hospital; malaria, tuberculosis and trachoma have been stopped
He was asked to run the new Trachoma Centre in Benghazi; malaria, tuberculosis and trachoma have been stopped
He went to Cairo to train; measles has been stopped
He qualified as a doctor; tuberculosis has been stopped
questions.correct_answer: He was asked to run the new Trachoma Centre in Benghazi; malaria, tuberculosis and trachoma have been stopped
questions.explanation: In 1973 he was asked to run the new Trachoma Centre in Benghazi. He became Senior Surgeon at Tripoli Central Hospital in 1987. He says: 'Through hard work, we have at last stopped the terrible diseases of yesterday — malaria, tuberculosis and trachoma.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027
questions.source_detail: Lesson: Huge changes in Libyan health care

questions.question_text: In 'Discovering Yemen', how should you describe the picture?
options: Start with the two four-wheel-drives in the foreground, then the things further away in the distance
Start with the mountains in the distance and end with the sky
Describe only the people in the cars
Start with the village and end with the cars
questions.correct_answer: Start with the two four-wheel-drives in the foreground, then the things further away in the distance
questions.explanation: The lesson says: 'Describe what you can see — first the two four-wheel-drives in the foreground and then the things further away in the distance.' Then learners discuss where the picture was taken and where the people might be going.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: Who is Faysal Hatem Al Qadhi, in the article 'Discovering Yemen'?
options: The writer of the article
The driver of the four-wheel-drive and owner of a little travel company
A doctor at a hospital in Sana'a
A teacher from the capital
questions.correct_answer: The driver of the four-wheel-drive and owner of a little travel company
questions.explanation: The article says: 'I became friends with Faysal Hatem Al Qadhi, the driver of the four-wheel-drive. I found out to my surprise that he was the owner of the little travel company that was taking us on this trip.'
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027

questions.question_text: What is Faysal's ambition for his travel company, and what does he hope for in a few years' time?
options: To own eight or ten four-wheel-drives in two years and take visitors all over Yemen; to have a wife and children and own a house
To become very rich and move to the capital; to buy a hotel
To sell the company and work for a newspaper; to travel abroad
To keep just one old four-wheel-drive; to live alone in the mountains
questions.correct_answer: To own eight or ten four-wheel-drives in two years and take visitors all over Yemen; to have a wife and children and own a house
questions.explanation: Faysal started his company fifteen months ago with just one old four-wheel-drive and now has two new vehicles. 'His ambition is to have eight or ten 4WDs two years from now and to take visitors all over Yemen.' He hopes in a few years he will have a wife and children; he doesn't want to be very rich, but hopes to own a house and give his family what they need.
questions.source: English Pupil's Course — Grade 12, Yemen, Sanaa 2027
